activities.title: Practical Context: Financial Order Book & Execution Queue

analogy.headline: Practical Context: Financial Order Book & Execution Queue
analogy.story:
High-frequency trading exchanges separate order ingestion from order matching. Ingestion uses a ring-buffer ArrayDeque for ultra-low latency FIFO processing. The active order book uses a PriorityQueue to match best bids and asks.

If a trader modifies an open order's price, the exchange cannot update the order in-place inside the priority heap without corrupting the order book. The old order must be explicitly cancelled and a new order inserted.

Understanding these distinct roles prevents costly data corruption.
analogy.keyTakeaway: Queue selection depends on workload: ArrayDeque for zero-allocation FIFO/LIFO, PriorityQueue for dynamic ranking. Mutating enqueued items breaks ordering invariants.

activities.title: Monotonic Deques, Anti-Patterns & Bug Diagnostics

keyTakeaways: Monotonic Deque preserves candidate elements in strictly decreasing order, solving Sliding Window Maximum in O(N) time
Never mutate comparison fields of objects inside PriorityQueue without re-insertion
Replace legacy java.util.Stack with ArrayDeque to eliminate synchronized lock contention
ArrayDeque and PriorityQueue reject null with immediate NullPointerException

activities.content:
### The Monotonic Deque Pattern

When tracking the maximum value over a sliding window of size $K$ across an array of length $N$, a brute-force approach requires $O(N \times K)$ comparisons. A **Monotonic Deque** stores indices whose values are strictly decreasing:
1. Before inserting index $i$, remove indices from the front that are older than $i - k + 1$ (expired from window).
2. Remove indices from the back whose corresponding values are $\le \text{nums}[i]$ (they can never be the maximum).
3. Insert index $i$ at the back.
4. The front of the deque always holds the maximum of the current window in **$O(1)$**.

Because each array element is pushed and popped at most once, total time complexity is strictly **$O(N)$**.

---

### Architectural Anti-Patterns Matrix

| Anti-Pattern | Root Problem | Consequence | Correct Pattern |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **In-place Heap Mutation** | Mutating comparison key after insertion | Heap invariant broken silently | Remove before mutating, then re-offer |
| **Legacy `java.util.Stack`** | Synchronized method overhead | Lock contention on multi-core systems | Use `Deque<T> = new ArrayDeque<>()` |
| **Passing `null` to ArrayDeque** | Implementation uses null as empty indicator | Immediate `NullPointerException` | Use `Optional<T>` or sentinel instances |
| **Iterating PriorityQueue** | Assumes sorted output | Incomplete partial heap order | Sequentially invoke `poll()` |

activities.title: Parentheses Validator with ArrayDeque Stack
activities.description: Trace a high-performance bracket nesting validator using ArrayDeque as a non-synchronized stack.

steps.description: Initialize ArrayDeque as a LIFO stack. Odd string lengths are rejected immediately in O(1).
For opening brackets, push expected closing brackets onto stack. For closing brackets, pop and verify.
Return stack.isEmpty(). An empty stack confirms all opened brackets matched in correct order.

questions.question: Why is java.util.Stack considered an architectural anti-pattern in modern Java?
options: It cannot store more than 100 elements
It extends Vector and synchronizes every operation on its intrinsic lock, causing severe thread contention
It uses recursion internally and causes StackOverflowError
It was removed from Java SE 17
questions.explanation: Stack extends Vector and synchronizes all methods (push, pop, peek), causing substantial performance degradation under concurrency. Deque with ArrayDeque is the official recommended replacement.

questions.question: What happens when you add an element to an ArrayDeque that exceeds its current capacity?
options: The oldest element is automatically dropped
The backing array doubles in capacity via doubleCapacity()
questions.explanation: ArrayDeque is an unbounded resizable array. When head == tail, it doubles its array size to accommodate new elements.

activities.title: Senior Engineer Interview: Queue vs Deque Architecture

qaList.question: Why does ArrayDeque outperform LinkedList for both Queue (FIFO) and Stack (LIFO) workloads?
qaList.answer: ArrayDeque outperforms LinkedList for three architectural reasons: 1. Memory Locality: ArrayDeque uses contiguous Object[] arrays, maximizing CPU L1/L2 cache prefetching; LinkedList allocates scattered Node objects that cause cache misses. 2. Allocation & GC Pressure: LinkedList allocates a Node wrapper per element on enqueue and discards it on dequeue; ArrayDeque reuses circular array slots with zero node allocation. 3. Memory Footprint: LinkedList requires 24-32 bytes of pointer overhead per element, whereas ArrayDeque requires only 4-8 bytes per array slot.

practiceProblems.title: Sliding Window Maximum (Monotonic Deque)
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Given an array of integers nums and a sliding window of size k moving from left to right, return the max sliding window array in O(N) time using an ArrayDeque.

practiceProblems.title: BFS Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Given an n x n binary matrix grid, return the length of the shortest clear path from top-left (0, 0) to bottom-right (n-1, n-1). All visited cells must be 0, and you can move in 8 directions. Return -1 if no path exists. Use a FIFO Queue<int[]>.

practiceProblems.title: Valid Parentheses Matching (ArrayDeque Stack)
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Given a string s containing characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid using ArrayDeque as a LIFO stack.

practiceProblems.title: Safe Priority Rescheduling with PriorityQueue
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a class MutableJobQueue managing jobs with mutable priorities. Because PriorityQueue does not auto-rebalance when priorities change in-place, implement a safe updatePriority(Job job, int newPriority) method that updates the priority and restores the heap invariant.

practiceProblems.title: First Non-Repeating Character in Stream
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Design a class StreamFirstUnique that reads characters one by one from a data stream and returns the first non-repeating character seen so far in O(1) amortized time per query using a FIFO Queue<Character> and a frequency map.
